description.narrative:
Malawi, Tanzania. The proposed project focuses on empowering young socio-economically marginalised women (especially young, unmarried mothers) with the aim of enhancing their economic self-sufficiency through income generating activities (IGAs) in combination with contextually relevant education on nutrition, sexual and reproductive health, and environmental management.
Exchange of competencies Several of the IGAs which SPRODETA has expertise in centre on the use of ‘Climate Smart Agricultural Technologies’, which enable beneficiaries to produce enough food to both meet their daily nutritional needs and to sell the surplus for profit. These technologies help enhance food security at the community level, and also enable the beneficiaries to be more resilient to the adverse effects of climate change on crop production.
SHALOM has well-established experience in promoting traditional vocational skills training such as tailoring, hairdressing and food preparation/ sale at the community level.
Participants from SPRODETA are thus expected to share their knowledge and skills on Climate Smart Agricultural Technologies with both SHALOM staff and their beneficiaries (primarily young, unmarried mothers), and at the same time to learn how to promote entrepreneurship using more traditional vocational skills training. At the same time, participants from SHALOM will train SPRODETA staff and beneficiaries on traditional vocational skills, and will similarly learn how to use and train others on Climate Smart Agricultural Technologies.
